ARK Invest founder, CEO, and Chief Investment Officer Cathie Wood stated her firm used the recent market pullback to purchase shares of Nvidia Corp., Tesla Inc., and Advanced Micro Devices Inc., while noting that cyclical technology and memory stocks fell sharply.

Concentrating on High-Conviction Technology

Wood told Wolf Financial Show host Goff Blackburg that ARK Invest sees "opportunity everywhere" following the recent technology sector sell-off. Wood stated that the firm responded to the market movement by altering its portfolio, explaining, "we concentrated our holdings towards our highest conviction names."

Wood specified that ARK Invest recently purchased shares in multiple technology companies. "We bought Tesla and SpaceX, we added to AMD, but we also added to Nvidia," Wood stated.

Wood characterized recent weekend news regarding Nvidia as "quite disappointing," but she pointed to comments from Elon Musk, who Wood quoted as saying, "We're speeding up our data centers in space."

She stated that Nvidia supported these orbital data centers, which she predicted will be a "huge source of demand" that Nvidia has secured with SpaceX in the near term. Furthermore, Wood stated that data center builders will have to "give more to these communities" rather than just taking from them to avoid derailing data center buildouts.

Cyclical Tech Stocks Slaughtered

Addressing the broader semiconductor and cloud markets, Wood noted that memory and cyclical technology stocks saw significant recent price drops.

Wood stated that ARK Invest is not typically exposed to commoditized or highly cyclical areas of the market, but she observed that "they have been slaughtered here."

She stated that market technicians described the recent price action as "three sigma moves," which Wood characterized as "very, very, very rare." Wood explained that if her firm's thesis regarding artificial intelligence (AI) is correct, these cyclical stocks are "probably buys."

Wood said that given the "thrashing" these stocks experienced, she would "probably be attracted" to them if she were an investor who traded that specific part of the market. She also stated she does not believe the "American renaissance is over" despite the recent market volatility.

title: Is AMD the Stock to Buy With Nvidia in Limbo?
detail:
Is AMD the Stock to Buy With Nvidia in Limbo?
Keithen Drury, The Motley Fool
Sat, November 21, 2026 at 7:00 AM CST 5 min read
AMD
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

With all the unknowns surrounding Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) right now, some investors are starting to wonder if Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) is the semiconductor stock to turn to instead. This is a natural progression because the two are competitors in the data center space.

Any analysis of a possible change should start by asking whether AMD is a viable alternative. Does AMD have problems of its own to contend with?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

My analysis suggests there's at least one issue that investors must watch out for, and I think it is definitive in determining which stock is the better pick right now. Let me explain.

Image source: Getty Images.

AMD is delivering solid results

AMD is commonly viewed as an alternative to Nvidia. Nvidia's data center products were more advanced than AMD's when the initial artificial intelligence build-out kicked off, and that allowed Nvidia to seize early market share. First-mover advantage can be difficult to overcome, and with a significant majority of data center computing infrastructure being built for Nvidia products, AMD has found itself in a deep hole.

However, the biggest problem AMD faces isn't hardware; it's software. Nvidia's CUDA software is considered better than AMD's ROCm software, although AMD has improved recently. Still, this is an advantage Nvidia holds over AMD, and it has created a gap unlikely to be closed.

AMD has seen increased success in the data center realm as clients look for cheaper alternatives to Nvidia GPUs, which can be quite expensive due to high demand. During the third quarter, AMD's data center revenue rose 97% year over year to $8.5 billion. However, because AMD also has significant consumer and embedded processor divisions, the results are a bit worse when the entire company is examined. Companywide, AMD's revenue rose 45% year over year to $13.4 billion. Considering that Nvidia is posting $100 billion-plus in quarterly revenue, AMD is a much smaller company.

Normally, being a smaller company is an advantage because it's easier to grow faster. But that hasn't been the case here. Nvidia has outpaced AMD's growth every step of the way, which is impressive considering the fact that it's almost 9 times larger than AMD. I think this speaks to the unbreakable lead that Nvidia has built from a technological and market-share standpoint.

title: Nvidia Just Issued a Major Warning to AMD and Intel Stock Investors
detail:
Nvidia Just Issued a Major Warning to AMD and Intel Stock Investors
Harsh Chauhan, The Motley Fool
Sat, November 21, 2026 at 6:14 AM CST 5 min read
NVDA
AMD
INTC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) released solid results for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 (which ended on Oct. 25) on Nov. 17 and backed its outstanding performance with impressive guidance.

Its data center business recorded healthy growth once again last quarter, and Nvidia's upgraded guidance for fiscal 2028 suggests that the segment will continue to move the needle substantially next year. However, a closer look at Nvidia's results suggests it is quickly gaining ground in a market where Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) and Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) are the dominant players.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Let's take a closer look at this particular business and check why Nvidia's progress in this space doesn't bode well for Intel and AMD.

Image source: Nvidia.

Nvidia's Vera CPUs are in terrific demand

The market for server central processing units (CPUs) has been growing rapidly amid the increasing adoption of agentic AI and inference applications. This explains why Nvidia decided earlier this year to offer its latest-generation Vera server CPUs as a stand-alone product to customers.

The company already had a server CPU before Vera, known as Grace, but it was available as part of rack-scale systems that integrated graphics cards, networking chips, memory, and other components into a single package. Nvidia's latest quarterly report is proof that its move into the stand-alone server CPU market is paying off.

The product has been adopted by leading hyperscalers, neocloud providers, and AI companies, including Oracle, Meta Platforms, OpenAI, CoreWeave, Nebius, and others. In fact, Nvidia has doubled down on the server CPU market by offering a CPU-based rack-scale server platform to handle agentic AI and inference applications.

Interim CEO Colette Kress remarked on the latest earnings call:

We continue to see very strong demand for Vera and expect total CPU revenue to more than double in fiscal year 2028.

Though the company didn't specify exactly how much revenue it generated from stand-alone sales of the Vera CPU last quarter, it noted on the fiscal Q1 earnings call that it expects $20 billion in revenue from this product in fiscal 2027. Assuming the estimate is still intact, Nvidia's Vera VPU revenue could jump to at least $40 billion next fiscal year.

This should set the alarm bells ringing for AMD and Nvidia investors.

Super Micro Computer raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook, expects AI related solutions to account for roughly 70% to 80% of sales, and is rolling out new AMD EPYC based all flash storage and H15 servers to support AI data center buildouts.

The business plans to lift production capacity to more than 8,000 racks per month by December 2026, including over 4,000 direct liquid cooled racks, which points to a heavy operational commitment to large scale AI infrastructure deployments.

With that investment narrative in mind, the focus now shifts to how Super Micro Computer's higher AI driven revenue outlook may reshape expectations.

Spotlight 53 AI infrastructure stocks that, like Super Micro Computer, are tied directly to the AI data center buildout and could benefit as rack-scale infrastructure spending ramps.

Super Micro Computer Investment Narrative Recap

To own Super Micro Computer, you need to believe the AI infrastructure buildout supports sustained demand for its rack scale server, storage, and cooling platforms, even with structurally thinner margins and a volatile share price. According to RogueEP, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community, this is a good stock in a tougher business, with value in disciplined assumptions rather than a smooth story.

Right now the key near term catalyst is execution on the huge AI focused revenue and rack capacity ambitions while managing funding that relies on higher risk borrowing and non cash heavy earnings. The biggest risk sits in any slowdown or pause in large AI data center deployments that could leave new capacity underutilized.

The most relevant update here is Super Micro Computer's launch of the H15 server portfolio and Petascale all flash storage platforms built around AMD's 6th Gen EPYC 9006 processors. These systems are designed for AI inference, large models, and high performance computing, and plug directly into the firm's rack scale DCBBS architecture.

This product family, including Helios and Helion racks, ties closely to the short term catalyst investors care about: turning the raised AI revenue mix outlook and 8,000 racks per month capacity target into shippable systems. Execution risk is clear. Management now needs to translate technical advantages, world record benchmark claims, and ecosystem partners into sustained orders and utilization.

RogueEP's own narrative arrives at a US$55.85 fair value for Super Micro Computer using a flat 0.0% annual revenue growth assumption and a future profit margin of 11.0%, treating the stock as a mature, steady earner rather than an aggressive AI growth story.

Key Takeaways

Cathie Wood's ARK Invest bought 49,745 shares of Advanced Micro Devices across two ETFs on Nov. 20, worth about $21 million at that day's close.

AMD is down 31% since Sept. 30, and its forward P/E of 28x is below its five-year average of 34x.

Analysts expect AMD's earnings to more than double in 2027. Getting there means winning AI business from Nvidia with chips Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing makes.

The numbers support the buy as long as AMD's Helios racks ship on schedule.

Cathie Wood's ARK Invest bought 49,745 shares of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD:NASDAQ) on Friday, Nov. 20, according to ARK's own daily trade email. At that day's close of $424.39, that's about $21 million.

The stock is 36% below its 52-week high. Much of AMD's case rests on winning a bigger share of an AI build-out that Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ) still leads, using chips made by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM:NYSE).

A small add after a big cut

The buy went into two funds: 39,157 shares for the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) and 10,588 for the ARK Next Generation Internet ETF (ARKW). That's 0.13% of each fund. The $21 million is the shares times Friday's close, since the email lists the portfolio changes ARK's team made but doesn't give a price.

It's a small trade next to what ARK already owned. The $17 billion firm's 13F for the quarter ended Sept. 30, filed Nov. 13, showed 675,668 AMD shares worth $413 million. That was 2.4% of its 13F stocks and its 14th-biggest position. It also came after ARK cut its AMD share count by 52% during the quarter. Since Sept. 30, AMD has fallen 31%.

Two November headaches

AMD had news of its own this month. On Nov. 16, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security put out an interim rule that requires licenses for advanced US AI chips shipped to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, and AMD's Instinct GPUs are covered. Then on Nov. 19, AMD fell 8% after Hunterbrook Media reported that IEIT Systems, a company on the Commerce Department's Entity List, had put newer AMD firmware into its BIOS updates. Hunterbrook's affiliate is short AMD. Hunterbrook says its findings don't show an export-law violation, and AMD said on Nov. 20 that the claims "misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships." ARK's buy came on the same day the Nasdaq 100 fell 6%.

Cathie Wood's ARK sold 135,760 NVIDIA shares from two ETFs on Friday, worth about $17 million at Friday's close.

AMD's latest quarter and TSMC's new spending point to AI chip demand that's still growing, and at this price NVIDIA looks like a stock worth holding.

Cathie Wood's ARK Invest sold some NVIDIA (NVDA:NASDAQ) on Friday, a day when chip stocks dragged the Nasdaq-100 down 6%.

AMD (AMD:NASDAQ) was among the chipmakers that fell, even though its data center sales nearly doubled last quarter. And Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM:NYSE), which makes NVIDIA's chips, just approved about $40.9 billion more for new capacity.

The sale itself is a trim

ARK's daily trade email for Friday lists 102,529 shares sold from the ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK), 0.09% of that fund, and 33,231 from the ARK Next Generation Internet ETF (ARKW), 0.11% of it. That's 135,760 shares in all, or about $17 million at Friday's $125.53 close. (We worked that out as shares times the close, since ARK doesn't say what it got.) The email lists the adjustments its investment team made, so it may not be every trade ARK placed.

For scale, ARK's 13F for the quarter ended Sept. 30, filed Nov. 13, showed 2.56 million NVIDIA shares worth $585 million, 3.4% of its 13F stocks and its fifth-largest holding. title: How Biden’s former aide sparked a $100bn stock market sell-off
detail:
How Biden’s former aide sparked a $100bn stock market sell-off
Louis Goss

AMD
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Sam Koppelman (C) with Amanda Seyfried (L) and Amy Koppelman. Koppelman, a former Biden speechwriter, is very much part of New York's liberal elite - Getty/Noam Galai

Walking down a street in New York filming a video, Sam Koppelman was about to detonate a $100bn (£76bn) bomb underneath Wall Street's largest tech companies.

In a short video posted on X, the 30-year-old former speechwriter for Joe Biden said he had big news which was about to rock the AI sector.

He revealed that his hedge fund, Hunterbrook Capital, had published a new investigation into Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), a Silicon Valley tech giant.

The lengthy report alleged that AMD had continued to supply microchips to a Chinese server manufacturer, IEIT Systems, after the Asian group was blacklisted by US authorities.

AMD has denied any wrongdoing, claiming Hunterbrook's report "misrepresents AMD's business practices and relationships".

However, its publication triggered a $100bn slump in the share price of the chip giant, contributing to a gloom engulfing the tech sector after the Nvidia scandal.

But who is Koppelman? And how did he and his hedge fund cause a tech crash?

The fund was launched two years ago and described itself as a "new kind of investigative newsroom", which makes money by trading on stories it uncovers. Often by "shorting" companies to profit when their share prices fall.

Koppelman started the firm with Nathaniel Horowitz, his friend from Harvard University.

The two founders had graduated from the Ivy League institution only a few years ago and might well be considered scions of America's liberal elite.

Koppelman, a native New Yorker, is the son of Brian Koppelman, the film and TV writer who wrote the 2007 film Ocean's 13 starring George Clooney and Brad Pitt.

Hollywood star Matt Damon is said to have written a recommendation to Harvard in favour of Koppelman.

His school, the Ethical Culture Fieldston School, is also well known as one of New York's best. He once even dated Maude Apatow, the American actress who is the daughter of Judd Apatow and Leslie Mann.

Horowitz, meanwhile, is the son of two Pulitzer Prize-winning writers. Tony Horwitz, his father, is best known for his investigations into the conditions of America's low-paid workers, while Geraldine Brooks, his mother, won the prize for her novel March, about the US civil war.

Sam Koppelman once dated Maude Apatow, the the daughter of Judd Apatow and Leslie Mann - Startraks Photo/Shutterstock

He attended school in Martha's Vineyard, the small island off the coast of Massachusetts where Barack Obama now owns an $11.75m holiday home, before studying Molecular and Cellular Biology.

He went on to start a series of biotech startups, focused on making treatments for diseases including pancreatic cancer and Type 1 diabetes, with the backing of some of the world's biggest pharmaceutical firms.
